description:
Radio details for one pass of a satellite over a location: its known downlink (and uplink) frequencies, the Doppler swing, when to tune to what (at 10 and 30 degrees up and at closest approach), and a table of at most 40 evenly spaced rows for pointing an antenna and tuning a radio. To choose a satellite or pass first use find_best_pass with mode radio, or find_passes; for a sky chart of the pass use get_pass_chart.

It uses the first pass that climbs above minElevation within windowHours (default 48), or with time the pass peaking nearest it (past or future, within 30 days of the elements' epoch). If there is none, window is null and message says why; the downlinks are still listed. A satellite that never sets here (geosynchronous) gets the next 24 hours instead. frequencyMHz picks the downlink; by default it is the one SatNOGS stations heard most recently, else the catalog's.

Predictions come from published elements: the transmitter's own offset is unknown, so compare the curve's shape. passUrl opens this pass on seeksat.com on the same frequency, and its Radio chart downloads the full table as CSV. Reception data is from SatNOGS Network (CC BY-SA 4.0). Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none.

frequencyMHz.description: the downlink to compute Doppler for, in MHz. Default: the satellite's default known downlink.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

minElevation.description: lowest elevation that counts: a pass must climb above it, and rise and set are when it crosses it, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90). Default 10.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss". e.g. "so-50" or 27607.

time.description: a time near the wanted pass's peak (e.g. from find_passes), past or future. Default: the next pass. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

windowHours.description: how far ahead to look, in hours, up to 240 (10 days). Default 48. How far past the start to look for a pass.
